2607.18883.title: RAMP: Recognition parametrisation by Amortised Message Passing
2607.18883.paper_summary: A central aim of unsupervised learning is to uncover latent factors that explain dependencies among observations. Probabilistic models typically achieve this by introducing multiple latent variables linked through a graph of conditional relationships, with distributional parameters and their dependence learnt from data. Learning relies either on distributional choices that allow tractable belief propagation, or on approximations that scale poorly with model size and complexity. We build on the recently developed recognition-parametrised modelling paradigm to propose an alternative approach: RAMP, a method that implicitly defines latent structure by learning a flexible, nonlinear, amortised message-passing framework. We show that RAMP enables efficient likelihood-based recovery of latent-variable distributions within expressive nonlinear models acting on complex high-dimensional data.
2607.18883.paper_summary_zh: 一個無監督學習的核心目標是揭示解釋觀察之間依賴關係的潛在因素。<lb/> 機率模型通常通過引入多個潛在變量，這些變量通過條件關係的圖形相連，來實現這一點，並從數據中學習分佈參數及其依賴性。<lb/> 學習依賴於允許可處理的信念傳播的分佈選擇，或依賴於隨著模型大小和複雜性增長而表現不佳的近似。<lb/> 我們基於最近開發的識別參數化建模範式，提出了一種替代方法：RAMP，一種通過學習靈活的、非線性的、攤銷的消息傳遞框架來隱式定義潛在結構的方法。<lb/> 我們展示了RAMP能夠在對複雜高維數據進行表達性非線性模型時，有效地基於似然恢復潛在變量分佈。
